thread:
sara (product): quick question — we're designing a saved-query UX that also expresses routing hints and quota preferences. should those live inside the saved query or be a separate 'routing overlay'?
kevin (eng): my vote is metadata on the saved query. simpler API: one GET returns query+route-hints. but need to be careful about permissioning (who can change routing).
liam (devex): +1 metadata. UX-wise, users expect 'save' to capture everything they see. if routing is a separate concept it'll confuse people.
anya (analytics): we also need telemetry flags. when a saved query includes routing overrides, tag all resulting telemetry with that saved_query_id + routing_variant so we can backfill quality/cost impacts.
michael (platform): technical caveat: some routing hints are dynamic (quota-aware fallbacks). storing static hints could break autoscaling fallbacks. maybe store preferred hints + a flag "allow_fallbacks": true/false.
sara (product): good call. proposed minimal model: saved_query.metadata.routing = {preferred_cluster, cost_priority, allow_fallbacks}. any objections?
kevin (eng): that works. API sketch: 
```json
{
  "id": "sq_...",
  "query": "route:transactions AND model:gpt-medium",
  "metadata": {
    "routing": {"preferred_cluster": "dedicated-eu-1", "cost_priority": "low", "allow_fallbacks": true}
  }
}
```
liam (devex): UX considerations: show a compact chip next to saved query label: "routing: dedicated-eu-1 (fallbacks on)". clicking opens full routing editor. also indicate quota headroom in the list (e.g., colored dot).
anya (analytics): for telemetry we should emit: saved_query_id, routing.variant, routing.runtime_decision (served_by, fallback_reason), token_cost, latency. that allows cost/regression dashboards.
michael (platform): +1. also need to define how quota buckets map to UI. i suggest we show both per-route quotas and per-project reserved capacity, with hover explaining which bucket was used.
kevin (eng): implementation note — backend will accept a saved_query.routing object and treat it as "preferred". runtime will consult policy: if bucket/region matches and capacity>threshold then honor, else record fallback and choose best-effort.
sara (product): rollout UX: when a saved query with routing is newly allowed for a customer, show a measured canary option: "apply to X% of traffic" and surface telemetry in Console -> Saved Query detail.
liam (devex): small copy suggestion for canary modal: "Apply routing override to N% of executions to validate cost and quality impact." include quick links to rollback.
kevin (eng): edge case: exporting saved queries. should exports include routing metadata by default? security might prefer stripping.
michael (platform): export should include it but mark it encrypted/annotated if it references private clusters. default: include everything, but warn on import for mismatched infra.
anya (analytics): for dashboards, create a default "Saved Query Impact" dashboard that aggregates token_cost, latency, and fallback_rate for the last 7/30 days. make it accessible from saved query page.
sara (product): consensus forming: 1) store routing hints in saved_query.metadata, 2) include allow_fallbacks flag, 3) emit telemetry tags, 4) canary apply UI, 5) export includes routing but warns. any blockers?
kevin (eng): one blocker — we need auth checks: only users with "routing.update" can modify routing metadata. will sync with auth team.
liam (devex): another UX note: when a saved query's routing can't be honored at runtime, surface a lightweight inline warning in Console results: "Requested routing not available — used fallback (reason)". small orange warning line.
michael (platform): ops-bot note: queued capacity alerts will be emitted when fallback_rate > 5% for 10m. tagging will include saved_query_id.
ops-bot: (system) Alert rule created: saved-query-fallback-rate > 5% over 10m -> notify #incidents and #product.
anya (analytics): last thing — add a telemetry dimension for "saved_query.source" (ui/manual/api) so we can filter noise.
sara (product): great — i'll write a short RFC summarizing model + API sketch + UX mockups and ping this thread. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
